title: Bind one selected Toom candidate to its dirty-input interface
body:
## Result

The first nine-climb group from the event-window model used in Gonzalo Mier's #3974 is an invertible 4,608-dimensional linear operator on nine independent dirty payloads. This package binds that actual group to its exact frames, incoming forms and serialized Clifford recipes, then rejects a precise same-width Toom-only coefficient interface.

The first eight registers `546,560,547,568,548,558,549,570` climb from frame 0 to `[459]`; register 464 climbs from frame 0 to `[75]`. Their actual incoming forms have a nine-by-nine identity minor. The selected receipt explicitly covers every arbitrary data/helper column, and the verifier proves the actual entry prefix is invertible: 7,344 shears, 56 nonzero scales, 464 typed frame adapters and 240 invertible monomial pre-wrappers; no clears or copies. The two 512-dimensional operators are reconstructed on all 1,024 basis columns, with exact global phase, halving and Gram matrices.

- A fixed-factor Toom module receives at most 1,536 input dimensions.
- Even allowing both affine coefficient triples and direct decoder access to both triples provides at most 3,072 dimensions, below 4,608.
- The ordinary affine decoder reading only five product blocks has output-image dimension at most 2,560, a deficit of 2,048.

These are explicit interface restrictions. Five child calls in an arbitrary circuit do not imply them. Retained productive inputs, bypasses, wider coefficients or a different recursive primitive change the contract; dimension deficits are not native-cost or child-count lower bounds. No implementation or kappa improvement is claimed.

A constructive alternative is also checked: the first eight maps equal `I_8 tensor T_[459]`, realized by the same frame on 12 bits with 4,096 payload coordinates. Its Fourier rank remains 1; this does not establish a unit-priced rank-eight child. Its larger payload and complete native invoice remain open.

## Evidence and scope

Base is freshly fetched canonical main `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, priority revision 6. Only `research/selected-toom3-typed-block` is added. Exact package commit is `e8ed7160e6ce18a13f94a541a9bfbfe1127e9048`.

Registered normal and optimized Python replays pass, including exact source pins, literal event/window binding, input minor, all 1,024 basis columns, Gram matrices, the eight-lane Clifford identity and four failure controls. Exact publication-byte/source-history checks and the official portable export check pass. Both normal and optimized runs also pass from a fresh Git-free export with empty PATH and all 10 files read-only; before/after hashes are unchanged. This is a scoped interface obstruction, not a complete supplier audit or formal-kernel proof.

Entry overlap covered 679 open PR bodies plus rendered active/handoff Discussions; the 08:13 UTC publication checkpoint covered 691 open PR bodies with no typed-Toom collision; broader Discussion, closed and private coverage remains partial. #3974, #1817, #1779 and #1836 were read at their live heads. The distinct companion task on two-register rank-two intertwining does not supply this nine-register Toom binding.

## Credit and next obligation

Credit Gonzalo Mier/#3974; Josie Elliston/#1817; Jose Manuel (@jmbarrancoml, credited in #1779 submitted via 1337isnot1337); Arham Tahir/#1605; Discussion #1987 contributors; and the selected #1094/Clifford/PR514/PR433 source lineage, including Rohan Arun, Jeremy Kothe and Hao Yan. Prepared for Clear1nsight with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0; no independent human acceptance claimed.

title: Construct a P104 dyadic tensor code and price repeated Gram stages
body:
This changes the representation premise behind #3961: one invertible Gaussian-dyadic code retains all 21,632 data fields across both logical P104 Gram stages. With `U=[[I,B],[0,I]]`, `L=U_r U_c^-t` and `(Xhat,Yhat)=(LX,L^-tY)`, the transformed coefficients are `P_r M_c` and `M_r P_c`, `M=UU^t`. The code is shared at the internal boundary, retains the kernel payload, and restores fixed X/Y slots without division by 13.

The package supplies literal scalar words with entry and exit charged. Against its specified uncoded reference, two repeated **uncorrected Gram pairs** save 110,592 unit additions and 33,280 halves/restoring doubles each; one pair loses 104,448 additions. This is a common-chart protocol comparison, not a full-caller or native-cost improvement. Other uncoded factorizations may amortize too.

The full identity caller still requires coded coefficients `N_r M_c` and `M_r N_c`, `N=M^-1`. Each omitted side term has rational rank 10,816; that is algebraic rank, not a native tariff lower bound. The proof derives the ordered physical chart conjugates and records the unresolved native code, actual repeated consumer, identity completion, helpers, ownership, routing, precision and complete gate. No actual adjacent completed P104 pair is claimed and no selected-frontier files change.

A separate ring obstruction distinguishes this construction from a free spectral split: `A tensor A` has rank 64 modulo 13, while the proposed product `169 P_r P_c` vanishes. Thus bank-separate invertible Gaussian-dyadic codes cannot realize that particular normalization. General bank-mixing codes and changed alphabets are outside the obstruction.

body:

title: Research: screen generic rational joint-plane supports
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Extends the exact two-plane decoder screen from binary coefficient values to generic rational coefficients. It enumerates all 65,536 4x4 support matrices, retains the 37,823 structurally nonsingular ones, and derives each generic inverse support from the perfect-matching condition on its 3x3 cofactors. These induce 439 source/reader signatures. The 391 signatures from invertible 0/1 matrices are all recovered; 48 additional generic signatures appear.

We price all 439 signatures on all 1,540 pairs of certified planes (676,060 cases). Every pair has minimum copy invoice 8, equal to four separate rank-two messages; there are zero strict improvements. The determinant/cofactor polynomial argument proves that every enumerated generic signature is realized by rational coefficients.

This is a scoped negative result for generic rational four-message bases across two fixed planes. It excludes neither specially tuned rational coefficients with cofactor cancellation nor overcomplete decoders, mixing three or more planes, coefficient scaling overhead, changed multi-array primitives, or physical routing/restoration. No replacement coverage law, supplier or kappa improvement is claimed; selected kappa is unchanged.

## Task and overlap

Base: freshly fetched canonical main `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, priority revision 6. Task `coverage-law-change`, **changed scope** to an exact generic-rational support screen for the fixed two-plane decoder interface.

The immediate predecessor is [PR #3990](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3990), which exhausts invertible 0/1 coefficient matrices. This PR rederives that 391-signature family as a control and adds the 48 generic rational support signatures; it has no source-code dependency on that open PR. Earlier related interface work includes [Discussion #1587](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1587), [PR #2126](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2126), and the `paired-plane-native-payload` independent-block invoice, which leaves cross-plane mixing open.

A targeted query for `generic rational two-plane decoder`, `generic inverse support patterns` and `cofactor cancellation encoder` found no external exact-term matches in the complete cached snapshot (690 open PRs and 2,580 Discussions, fetched at 08:05–08:06 UTC on 2026-10-19). The only local hit was this package’s own `TASK.json`. A live refresh failed because `api.github.com` was unreachable; the snapshot predates PR #3990, which was reviewed directly. The broad card terms surface many related checks. These limits do not establish novelty.

## Validation

On CPython 3.12, direct normal and optimized replays and the registered package replay passed:

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/rational-joint-support-screen/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -B research/rational-joint-support-screen/verify.py
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/rational-joint-support-screen --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/rational-joint-support-screen
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/rational-joint-support-screen --check-source-history
```

The replay cross-checks structural nonsingularity by permutation search and subset DP, checks the 22,560 invertible binary matrices and their 391 support signatures, computes pairing ranks with independent row/column elimination, and reproduces the full result receipt. Publication-byte and source-history checks passed for commit `e8551f2b0d13f292e53559237ea8387585f94257`. No native replay, physical implementation, Lean proof or selected cold replay is claimed.

## Credit

Credit the selected paired-plane matching/endpoint lineage and the prior binary decoder screen in PR #3990. Prepared for Gonzalo Mier with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. No independent human review is claimed. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

Can special rational assignments on cofactor-zero varieties yield a cheaper support signature? The next step is to classify realizable cofactor zero patterns while keeping the determinant and every supported coefficient nonzero, starting with supports whose minors have multiple matching monomials. Any saving still needs an exact coefficient witness, a priced native interface and a restoration schedule. See `TASK.json` for the blocker.

title: Research: exact Toom-3 five-product profile screen
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Constructs and verifies the exact five-product Toom-3 factorization for multiplying degree-two polynomials. The verifier reconstructs the rational interpolation map and checks all nine input monomial pairs.

A hypothetical block replacing nine selected rank-one recursive products with five saves four rank-one units. On the pinned complex profile, 64 realized blocks would clear the task card's five-percent local-ceiling gate; 210 would move the complex-side transfer cap above 0.002. At 254 hypothetical blocks, the local complex-side ceiling is [0.002086688163384, 0.002086688163385], corresponding to a local κ cap near 0.002082342962972. The selected forward and backward traces each contain 254 disjoint groups of nine rank-one climbs eligible under the phase-local movement model from #1817.

These are screening results, not a selected-provider construction: no group is bound to Toom coefficient inputs or outputs, and copies, scratch, dirty-state restoration, precision and native hosting remain unpriced. A direct scalar schedule costs 19 additions and 13 rational scales per hypothetical block.

This PR records a useful partial result and a negative global result. Under the retained transfer, the unchanged bit provider caps overall κ at 0.001730427469824, so the Toom-3 complex-side screen alone cannot reach overall κ > 0.002. Selected κ remains 0.001672660197076918. No new κ or supplier claim is made.

Base: freshly fetched canonical main `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`. Task `complex-rank-shape-decoder`, **changed scope** to screen a five-product bilinear convolution factorization and its selected-profile effect.

title: Research: screen selected rank-two macro fusion
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Screens direct fusion of two successive rank-one frame climbs into a selected rank-two child recipe in the pinned complex provider. If the composition were exact, the recursive charge of two rank-one calls would fall by the factor 2^-a for a > 0.

Each orientation has 2,412 rank-one climbs and 1,441 successive same-register links. Thirty-five links have a matching rank-two recipe for their combined endpoint frames. Every one of those 35 candidates has intervening scalar work on the same register (10 with one touch, five with two, 20 with five). No pair can be replaced directly while preserving the recorded scalar schedule.

Linearity suggests moving a post-add climb to the add's source operand. Across all 100 candidate/add-operand instances, none of those source registers already receives the exact same rank-one frame transition anywhere in the trace. The simple route that reuses an existing matching call is therefore absent too.

This is a scoped negative result for direct pair replacement and same-key call reuse, not a no-go theorem for redesigned macrocircuits. Matching endpoint frames does not prove that a rank-two child equals two rank-one children plus the intervening operations. No new supplier, exact macro equivalence or κ improvement is claimed; selected κ remains 0.001672660197076918.

title: Prove P112 six-dimensional incidence floor and exclude two literal C5 callers
body:
Two literal historical C5 callers have total support budgets of 156 and 148. This package proves that eleven pieces spanning six P112 code dimensions need at least **164 support incidences**, excluding `5^10,7` and `5^9,6^2` with margins **8 and 16** over every characteristic-zero field. Their quotient dimension is five under the explicitly inherited second generalized-weight bound.

The new argument pairs generalized Hamming weights with root-matroid fibers and singleton/pair incidence. A common-zero correction raises the naive 152 floor to 158; pair incidence strengthens it to `164 + 4z`, where `z` coordinates vanish on the same six-dimensional code subspace. It permits arbitrary coefficients, cancellations and dependent pieces in the general lemma. Actual caller pieces retain their original independence hypotheses.

Evidence:

- Exact rational enumeration of all 4,900 rank-two and 85,680 rank-three root-spanned flats, with closure digests and attaining controls.
- Separate 23-pattern Gram certificate for the rank-three root cap of six lines.
- All 393 positive definite rank-four Gram patterns and 245,625 integral target vectors certify the pair-fiber cap of twelve; Bareiss and permutation-determinant implementations agree on the complete case digest.
- Both named rows pass the unchanged PR3154 filter. Registered optimized replay, meaningful boundary/actual-code/receipt-mutation controls, committed-source/history checks and read-only Git-free export replay pass.
- A separate agent audited scalar extension, common-zero counting, quotient binding and the pair-incidence inequality. This is assisted-team corroboration, not independent human or proof-kernel acceptance.

Reproduce: `python3.12 -I -Werror -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-six-dimensional-incidence`.

body:
## Problem and result

PR #3554 left two conditional handoffs: identify an actual physical provider of its coefficient interface, and identify a required legal readout of its five-readout kernel. This PR answers them with one source-bound consumer audit against the unchanged PR #2586 word.

The original coefficient witness `a44 = delta15` prepares `Y91 = p, Y90 = -p`. It fails the actual full-word contract at zero-based event **1099**, `D1 += Y90/4` in frame `[381,241,2]`. At address **10**, the donor is `(-2,0)`, requiring real increment **-1/2**. All 1,099 earlier events complete exactly, with no completed event output outside B9. This binds an actual omitted read, rather than merely failing a sufficient product-domain condition.

There is also an admitted observable family. For **every `u in B9`**, set `Y91 = 4u, Y90 = -4u` and all other initial public banks to zero. A written induction, supported by the complete scalar denominator certificate and credited native preservation/covariance, proves exact execution through all **5,398 events** and

$$\rho_5(y)=0,\qquad X0_{\mathrm{final}}=-2A_Fu.$$

Thus no function of the five readouts alone can supply this required X0 endpoint, even on the strong domain. The actual path is Y90 to D1, the eighth collector's Q0, G0, and X0. The late X0 sign at event **5086** is essential. The displayed D27 transient at 1817 to 1819 has no intervening direct reader.

The unchanged word has **728 Y writes, all bank-local native transports**. It cannot materialise the coupled K encoder under a direct one-bank-per-independent-coefficient identification, even after relabelling. All **104 final Y frames have dimension eight**, while the logical caller returns its coefficient fields in empty frames. External preparation, virtual coefficient access, and adapters remain possible, with an explicit physical contract and complete price.

Only `research/p104-kernel-consumer/` is added. Each of 103 active Y fields is halved once, used for its A column through signed unit ADDs, and immediately doubled back. Y1 is unused by the prefix but remains required by the projection. The 52 X outputs and 41 omitted N/G banks then move to the full frame.

The **local** prefix accepts all 93 dirty fields in B9 and all 104 Y fields in 4B9, with temporarily writable Y access. body:
## Problem and result

The retained outer layout and the newer actual-width root choose different chunk widths. The outer construction has `d=floor(p^(1/40))`, selects `g=d-1` axes, and lays out chunks using `K_d=floor(d^(1/500))`. PR #3599 instead computes `K_g=floor(g^(1/500))`. At every nontrivial boundary `d=k^500`, the two widths are `k` and `k-1`. This changes the complete array extent and the selected physical bits. Enlarging a left extent to hide the cardinality mismatch still applies the wrong tensor.

This package proves the mismatch and constructs a matched layout, inverse layout and complete descriptors using `K_g`. It covers every common offset, top and bottom elementary round, singleton and mixed axes, and both directions. The common rounds already select consecutive equal-sized chunks, so this repair needs no additional general-support router. Layout movement and component-order conversion remain charged, and the old outer constructor still needs a correctly typed replacement.

The written counterexample survives final rounding: an admitted unit-disk impulse produces different p-grid outputs under the intended and naively substituted tensors. Exact checks also distinguish the production floor thresholds, including the actual caller's precisions divisible by six. The matched `K>=k` threshold is `(k^500+1)^40`, rather than `k^20000`.

## Conditional layer theorem and published diagonal join

The proof establishes the actual caller's record-size and dimension admission. Completed normalised butterflies, truncation towards zero, and signed polynomial permutations preserve the unit disk on the p-grid throughout all rounds. Thus `w=p+2` admits every required signed negation. PR #3611 already supplies the one-packet width observation; this result proves its complete-round implication.

With `T=Mr` coefficients, the retained ordinary movement exponent `tau=99830289/10^8`, and root exponent `alpha=99827101/10^8`, the conditional bound is

```text
O(T p [d K + p K^(tau-1) + ell g^alpha log p]).
```

The remaining caller must provide the actual root/rounded return and a complete lifecycle bill `Q <= C M R(rw+A+p^3)+poly(p)`, with fixed simultaneous buffers, restored borrows and heads, and consumed previous outputs. title: Research: project a 96-output F17 demand and screen its retained-centre budget
body:
PR[2512](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2512) actually demands 96 ordinary `y1_U` arrays in `F_U1=F17`. This projects PR[2707](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2707)'s complete inverse onto that endpoint, using all 112 current Y fields and no early T retention or current X reads. The changed 1,410-event word returns the 96 owned outputs, clears sixteen owned full-cover temporaries and eight owner-private scratch fields, and leaves every borrowed input untouched.

The complete local invoice is **112 H1**, **224 native wrappers**, **208 cover maps**, 560 unit ADDs, 384 quarter ADDs and 144 CLEARs: **9,376 real scalar primitive allowance**. Relative to the full 224-output decoder, this genuinely removes 224 H1, 448 wrappers, 256 maps and 16,464 scalar allowance. It drops future-logger reversal, the F0 inverse and unrelated recovery; it does not lower the tariff of unchanged recursive calls.

The budget conclusion changes in a material way:

- **The old rank-eight-waived obstruction does not extend to this reduced demand.** Its favorable moment is [0.999995759681, 0.999995760274].
- Keeping the reported eight H8 per call under the same centre 64 pair-rate model instead gives **[1.000023149708, 1.000023150305] > 1**, even with every physical overhead free.

title: [Lean] Link an end-to-end proof of multiplication below n log n
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Add a pointer under “Research notes and verification contributions” to [Dan Brown](https://github.com/jdb19937) and [Kenny Daniel](https://github.com/platypii)'s end-to-end Lean proof of integer multiplication below n log n on Mathlib's finite Turing machines.

The fixed finite Mathlib machine multiplies every pair of binary-encoded natural numbers in worst-case time `O(n (log n)^(1−κ))` with **κ = 127238784 / 2^46 ≈ 2^-19.0770**. The theorem includes the complete compact runtime, all-input correctness, and the actual machine-step bound. This is an asymptotic exponent bound, not a measured execution speedup.

Correctness and runtime are proved without remaining algorithmic or analytic assumptions. The theorem's transitive axiom dependencies remain exactly `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`.

## Task and overlap

Documentation pointer to an external completed proof, based on upstream `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`. This does not establish the selected conditional saving κ = `0.001672660197076918` or change the selected construction.

## Validation

The proof is pinned at [3e7d90a4](https://github.com/platypii/integer-mult-bounds-lean/tree/3e7d90a4bf39cad3fda42d622543b05ff4cc176e): [statement and machine model](https://github.com/platypii/integer-mult-bounds-lean/blob/3e7d90a4bf39cad3fda42d622543b05ff4cc176e/IntegerMultBounds/MathlibTM2/Statement.lean), [explicit and existential theorems](https://github.com/platypii/integer-mult-bounds-lean/blob/3e7d90a4bf39cad3fda42d622543b05ff4cc176e/IntegerMultBounds/MathlibTM2/Theorem.lean), and [completed-proof axiom audit](https://github.com/platypii/integer-mult-bounds-lean/blob/3e7d90a4bf39cad3fda42d622543b05ff4cc176e/CompletedProofCheck.lean).

The [CI run for this exact source](https://github.com/platypii/integer-mult-bounds-lean/actions/runs/39212691096) was pending when this description was updated.

Checked the README-only diff, whitespace, and agreement with the pinned theorem and audit entry point, and the rounded base-two exponent. No new Lean build or historical certificate replay was run for this documentation update.

Since #3190, a bin hosting `used` helper cells kept them on the recipe prefix `[0, used)`, and its idle remainder was the recipe suffix `[used, cap)`. After #3934:

title: Research: length-≤2 dest-in diverge census — four #3696 rejects not exhaustive (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Answers open question 2 of [#3696](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3696) under the [#2977](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2977)/[#3004](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3004) checker/exporter cascade. That PR showed dest-free gates always make Sym and Exp agree, named dest-in witnesses that diverge, and four B[0] `bad operands` rejects. OQ2 asked whether those four rejects are exhaustive for dest-in-sources divergence on the pinned word.

They are not. On the pinned tuned word, at B[0] destination `d=111` over `n=661` registers, Sym≠Exp for exactly **661** source lists of length at most 2 — namely all `[a,d]`. Only `self_even` and `dest_with_src` among the four named rejects lie in that set; `dup_src` and `self_once` agree.

This package also proves a dest-in closed form: Sym and Exp agree iff either `d ∉ srcs`, or else `count(d)` is odd and every non-`d` value has even multiplicity in the strict prefix before the last `d`. Dest-free agreement is used inside that form and is not republished as the claim. Every length-≤2 divergence fails operand distinctness and is rejected by the checker.

**No new kappa.** Selected κ stays `0.001672660197076918`. No production/schema adoption.

## Task and overlap

- Package: `research/selected-word-reject-exhaustion/`
- Tip: `8db402376a5604dcccd9a4db9072313253595f2d`
- Base: `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`
- Scope: **changed** — answer #3696 OQ2 with closed form + exact length-≤2 census

Closest prior: open [#3696](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3696). Soft overlap is a semantic successor (token ≈0.10 / line ≈0.33), not a ~0.9 dest-free retarget and not the deferred dest-absent corollary. Cascade priors #2977/#3004 leave alone.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/selected-word-reject-exhaustion/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -Werror -B research/selected-word-reject-exhaustion/verify.py
python3.12 -I -B research/selected-word-reject-exhaustion/independent.py
python3.12 -I -B research/selected-word-reject-exhaustion/test_package.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-word-reject-exhaustion
```

Expected:

```text
PASS_SELECTED_WORD_REJECT_EXHAUSTION len2_divergences=661 named_diverge=2 four_exhaustive=false no_new_kappa
PASS_SELECTED_WORD_REJECT_INDEPENDENT len2_divergences=661 named_diverge=2 four_exhaustive=false
PASS_SELECTED_WORD_REJECT_PACKAGE_TESTS
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/selected-word-reject-exhaustion outcome=completed
```

Default verify is read-only. Admission uses `need()` and still fires under `-O`.

## Credit

Credit [#3696](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3696) for the dest-free lemma, named rejects, and OQ2; Nick Petalas / #2977 and Kumagi / #3004 for the cascade; Dylan Crow exporter; eumemic symbolic checker; tuned PR589 word. Prepared by Wentao Li ([VictorLiwentao](https://github.com/VictorLiwentao), [@Is__Victor](https://x.com/Is__Victor)) with substantial AI assistance, under Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

1. Exact length-≤3 divergence count at the same destination?
2. Should schema docs separate divergence classes from distinctness rejects?

title: Research: census of staged entries on PR3734's other helpers; none found that pays (no new κ)
body:
This asks whether the staged-entry mechanism of #3605 (helpers 644/660) and #3734 (helper 544) lowers the hosted width of any **other** helper of #3734's word, from 9 to 8 or from 8 to 7, and whether it pays. It is stacked on #3734's head `fa041037a3374eaa08feeca0b26a5d6893194147` and adds only `research/staged-entry-census-3734/`. **No new κ.**

## Result

- **The identities exist.** Exact prefix identities (`P·v = v` for #3605/#3734, or the general form with releases `a = M_c v − e_h` into any register) exist for 25 width-8 and all 38 width-9 candidates whose blocking contacts are reads before the producer.
- **With the other frames fixed, no construction exists.** 9,862 (helper, raise, cut) cases per provider were tested, with releases allowed into any frame-compatible register, targets included. The same code rediscovers the three published cases on their parent words: 544 on #3682's word, 644 and 660 on #3133's word, with the same donors and coefficients.
- **With frames re-solved, only helper 472 reaches width 7.** Feasibility is decided by an exact minimal-assignment test: it is pointwise minimal among assignments keeping A, the entrances and the terminals, so its failure is a proof. 472 is staged by `624 −= 472` and `628 −= 472/2` before its producer B538, with entrance `span(429,51)`. It passes #3734's frame bill, hygiene and full arbitrary-dirty semantics on both providers.
  - Its frame cascade costs `{1:+15,2:−9,3:−2,4:+2}` per call.
  - An exact dual certificate adapted from #3815 shows that every owner fill of this inventory and bill, for any clock and any replica count, has root `< 0.0017305031`. The parent ceiling `0.001730578437266246818740` (attained by #3802/#3815) is `7.5e-8` higher.
  - In #3862's terms, 472's signature nets `−0.00154` per width unit; the 544 signature nets `+0.00326`.
- **The width-9 helpers fail as well.** Leaving the zero-frame compensation pushes a target out of its port hyperplane or over its cut level, for every placement tried.

**Why it fails.** For 544, 644 and 660, the donors' next frames already contained the raised entrance. For every other candidate, the producer's frame and the recipients' next frames meet only in the old entrance. The new direction therefore propagates and splits partner climbs. For 472, `{624, 628}` is the only donor set of size three or less.

## Verification

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/staged-entry-census-3734 --check-only
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/staged-entry-census-3734
python3 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/staged-entry-census-3734 --check-source-history
```

All three pass locally (CPython 3.12.14 on macOS arm64; the replay takes about 11 s, standard library only).

`verify.py` does the following:
- rebuilds the 472 word from #3734's words and compares it with the frozen words;
- runs the audits above, and rejects a flipped release and releases placed after the producer;
- shows that the pure retiming of 472's early read is scalar-correct but frame-infeasible;
- rebuilds 544, 644 and 660 on their parent words (#3605's parent is read from #3734's archive, with its digest checked);
- checks the exact certificate: tight to 1e-10, with the parent bracket and a perturbed dual as controls;
- authenticates the recorded census and recomputes its summaries.

The census itself (numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1) is recorded in `evidence/` with its commands. The optional `replay_subset.py` reruns a subset in about 2.5 min and reproduces the recorded rows exactly. It is not registered, because float decisions could differ across BLAS builds.

## Scope and limits

- **Sampled cuts.** 24 per helper plus the producer cut with fixed frames; 5 or 6 per helper with re-solved frames, with up to 4 placements per release recipient. Infeasibility is proved per placement.
- **What stays fixed.** Other entrances and terminals, the prelude and the native maps. Joint staged entries and clock changes are not searched.
- **472's frames are not proved optimal.** The certificate holds for the constructed frames. Two local optimisers (B; A+B) and a 4,200-slot retiming search find nothing better, but an exact frame solve of the 472 word was not run, and a cheaper assignment is not excluded.
- **#3945 (4→5 widening).** With the same cascade, 472 also loses about `7.5e-8` on the ideal ceiling. This is a float estimate from #3945's published profile; its words were not used.
- **Inherited.** All of #3734's conditional hypotheses. No selected-frontier change. If #3734 changes head, this needs a rebase and a rerun.

## Open next questions

1. Joint staged entries of two helpers whose donors overlap, as #3605 did for 644/660.
2. An exact frame solve of the 472 word on its nine cascade registers; absorbing the cascade by changing partner terminals; or 472 on #3945's word.
3. Every cut rather than a sample: a matter of compute.

The details are in `TASK.json`, `README.md` and `FINDING.md`.

## Credit

The staged-entry mechanism is due to Ross Richardson (#3605) and dataisfire (#3734). The frame bill and semantics are Sagar Thakrar's, from #3734's retained `audit_core.py` and `audit_verify.py`; `rational_price.py` is dataisfire's. The exact dual is adapted from #3815, and the width-unit prices are from #3862 (thakrarsagar) and #3890 (ToikY). Related but distinct work: #3933, #3886/#3941/#3942 and #3945.

Prepared by Erwan Secousses with substantial assistance from Claude (Anthropic, Claude Code). There is no independent human or formal review. Apache-2.0.

title: Negative result: +10% centre sharing at c* ≈ 0.0018433 needs 511 net complex rank-1 units (3.55/call, not 1.33); no admitted bit lever nets any of the 649 needed (no κ)
body:
## Statement

Planning bound and scoped proof. No construction, no κ claim, and not a multiplication theorem. The selected record is unchanged: κ = 0.001672660197076918 (#1094), complex-bound.

This prices the +10% centre-sharing route at the bit endpoint c\* = 921658892752012102303/5e23 ≈ 0.0018433. That endpoint is 1.0634x the current value, and PR1791 (centre-sharing-overhead-budget) derives it for +10% whole-bound κ. It also answers PR1791's open question 1. The bit side uses the actual PR589 histogram: deficit 10,272, m = 64, W = 28,416, T = 32, 288 calls, nine rank-7 copies per call, cst = 63. Every lever changes exactly one premise, and the surcharge is recomputed each time.

**Complex side (correcting PR1791 OQ1).** κ ≥ 1.1x selected requires the complex endpoint to reach c\* itself. PR1791's figure of ≥ 1.33 units per call is not enough. The requirement is a sharp **511 net rank-1 children** (510 fails), about **3.55 per call** over 144 calls. Necessity is asserted: κ(c\*−1e-24, c\*) < target ≤ κ(c\*, c\*). Under two-call sharing, the complex overhead budget at c\* is **4,079 rank-1 or 511 rank-8 children**, about **28.3–28.4 units per call**. That is an additive rank-1/rank-8 budget under PR1791's treatment; mixed ranks allow slightly more (PR1888).

**Bit side.** The requirement is **649 net rank-1 units**; 648 fails.
- Every admitted lever nets **≤ 0**:
  - (a) Halving depth 3/4 (idle cap 45 → 50/53) nets exactly 0. The recipe's idle windows are {7, 14, 28, 42}, so no child exceeds 42 < 45. Bridges delimit the windows, so no child can span two of them. PR1334's cap-50/53 columns and its HD-4 escape therefore cannot be reached by any recipe in PR1487's nine-stage class.
  - (a') Width-8 re-hosting nets exactly 0. This is certified by a concavity argument and re-certifies #1023 at c\*.
  - (b1) Rank-8 copy carriage nets −2,577.6.
- Clearing 649 needs a new word, decoder or coverage law. Sharp sizes:
  - (b2) Remove 93 of the 2,592 copies record-wide (92 fails). A uniform decoder change removes 288, one per call.
  - (b3) Bit-side two-call centre sharing (cst 31.5) gives +9,039.5, with overhead ≤ 8,391 rank-1, 1,203 rank-7 or 201 rank-42 children (29.1–29.3 per call).
  - (c) A second unpaid coordinate on ≥ 649 families. This is necessary for pure one-unit removal.
  - (d) ≥ 40 pure helper deletions per call (RANK1 model, stage-relaxed pass). 39 fails for every hosting. PR1043's TEMPLATE delta is exhausted at d = 19 with ≤ +170.4.
  - (e) Ideal in-window shapes in ≥ 52 of 288 calls (51 fails).
  - (f) Partial width-7 conversion clears only in #1023's window-free relaxation, at k = 71 per call. Under replica-local windows no k ≤ 74 clears (PR1736). The full all-439 conversion clears, but it needs a changed prefix (#1128).

## Milestone and decision informed

The milestone is a planning bound for `centre-path-sharing`, which is recursive-interfaces work. The package is filed under `bit-helper-contract` with a recorded scope change. The decision it informs:
- No admitted bit parameter lever makes two-call centre sharing part of a +10% route.
- On the complex side, the route needs ≥ 511 net rank-1 units, about 3.55 per call.
- On the bit side, it needs one of the new mechanisms above, at its stated size.
- Halving-depth 3/4 admission is worthless as a bit lever on nine-stage windows.

## Base, pins, reproduce

- Base: canonical main `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, priority revision 6. Pins are in `research/bit-endpoint-lever-budgets/SOURCES.json`, with sha1 and sha256 recorded.

```
python3 -I -B research/bit-endpoint-lever-budgets/verify.py && python3 -I -B research/bit-endpoint-lever-budgets/independent.py
```

Expected output (under a minute, standard library only):

```
PASS_BIT_ENDPOINT_LEVER_BUDGETS need_rank1=649 admitted_levers_max_net=0 copies_sharp=93 deletions_per_call=RANK1:40/TEMPLATE:None width7_windowfree_per_call=71 ideal_shape_calls=52 complex_need_rank1=511 no_new_kappa
PASS_BIT_ENDPOINT_LEVER_BUDGETS_INDEPENDENT signs=75 at c*-1e-24, c* and c*+1e-24 (levers.py interval arithmetic)
```

Other checks:
- `python3 -I -B -m unittest discover -s research/bit-endpoint-lever-budgets -p test_package.py` passes; 11 tamper cases are rejected, including a consistent-shift tamper that only the independent sign arithmetic catches.
- `scripts/research_package.py --check-only` passes, and so does the registered python3.12 replay (round 1).
- `verify.py` regenerates `RESULT.json` byte-identically.

## Certificates and negative controls

- **Exact arithmetic.** Sharp integers are computed exactly at c\*.
- **Independent second method.** `independent.py` rebuilds every boundary histogram with separate code and recomputes all 75 pass/fail signs with bit-revision3-levers-seed03/levers.py interval arithmetic (PR1334: atanh prime-chain ln, Taylor exp with remainder, outward rounding). It checks c\*−1e-24, c\* and c\*+1e-24. The lever definitions and hosting model are shared with `verify.py`; only the histogram code and the arithmetic are independent.
- **Negative controls.** Each of these fails:
  - 648 rank-1 children;
  - 92 copies;
  - 39 deletions per call;
  - 51 ideal-shape calls;
  - every budget + 1 child;
  - complex 510 rank-1, and complex budget + 1;
  - TEMPLATE at exhaustion;
  - width-7 at k = 70 (concavity bound);
  - the selected endpoints' next grid points;
  - κ at c\*−1e-24.

## Scope, assumptions, unresolved obligations

- Every passing row (b2, b3, c, d, e, f) is a pricing pass for a hypothetical word or decoder. None of these is paid:
  - the word or decoder itself;
  - the dirty-input endpoint and restoration;
  - hosting under the real stage windows;
  - the row-coefficient invoice and native precision/tape;
  - admission.
- (b3) also needs the bit analogue of PR1748's ownership/sink blocker.
- Rows (c) and (d) hold only within their stated models.
- Inherited: PR1791's endpoint model, the fixed-histogram bill and surcharge law, the coverage identity at fixed m and W, PR589's H1–H5, and the all-size, compiler, precision and analytic obligations.
- The PR1736 window bound (0.0018099 at k = 74) is cited, not re-asserted.
- PR1334's rank-8 (h = 8) and rank-16 rows are noted as uncertified estimates of about 50 and 34 calls.

## Search record

There was no search. Each lever is a one-parameter family, monotone because the bill is affine in the counts. Boundaries come from bisection or an exhaustive scan. Re-hosting optimality uses a concavity certificate.

## Credit, concurrent work and what this adds

Predecessors:
- PR1791 (rtyu193-rgb, centre-sharing-overhead-budget): the 649 requirement, OQ1 and the sharp-removal method.
- PR1334 (bit-revision3-levers-seed03): lever premises and interval arithmetic.
- Navinor's selected-suppliers-de-diagnostic: moment enclosures.
- Wronskode's frontier1042-invoice-audit-seed81 (#1112): bootstrap.
- PR589 and PR555: bit supplier and coverage law.
- PR1487 (bit589-recipe-floor).
- #1023 and PR1736: width-7 pricing and windows.
- #1281 (mightyOil): partial width-7 slot optima.
- #1128 (Ali Romman): bit-width-seven-boundary.
- PR2465 / PR1043 / PR1250 (bbMisk): deletions.
- PR1808 (JosieElliston): plane-port copy budgets.
- PR1888 (RossRichardson): mixed-rank overhead.
- PR3075 (navinor): the k = 2 charged costs, 4 ADD + 4 scratch CLEAR + 4 precision per call. Its charged costs fit inside the budget; eligibility and demand coupling remain the blockers.
- PR1708 (1337isnot1337) and PR1748 (ToikY): the complex two-call phase.
- r740-hosted-eleven row_bound: HD admissibility.
- r439-copy-path-sharing-barrier.

The README gives full heads.

Concurrent work: #3873 (Clear1nsight) bounds causal scalar-oracle centre sharing and audits the coverage ledger. That is a different object; neither prices bit levers at c\*.

New here:
- pricing at c\*;
- the slack-cap observation;
- the bit-side sharing budget;
- the sharp sizes;
- the complex-need correction (511 rank-1, 3.55 per call, against PR1791's 1.33).

Reviewed by 7 independent AI review passes in the same loop, across two rounds: reproducibility and negative controls; adversarial math and accounting, including a python-flint arb recheck at 320 bits; novelty, provenance and compliance; and a referee. Two revise rounds followed. No human has reviewed this.

title: Prove commutative caller obstruction for the integer-shear target
body:
PR3905 proves an exact four-call minimum for the integer-shear target B=X²Y² in F2[G]. This contribution resolves one caller-transfer obligation: every unital algebra map from F2[G] into a commutative F2-algebra sends B to 1. The exact relation XY⁻¹X=Y⁻¹XY⁻¹ forces UV=1. For the selected additive carrier F2[M3(Q)], the order-four relation, domain property and augmentation additionally force both generator images to 1.

The theorem permits arbitrary algebra images, including polynomial encodings. It concerns entrywise scalar-algebra transfer; noncommutative matrix carriers and other encoding contracts remain outside scope. PR3905’s formal minimum remains valid. No native implementation, supplier bill, new kappa, or frontier change is claimed.

Evidence:
- Written universal proof; exact source-bound relation checks.
- Registered Python 3.12.14 replay passes, including the unchanged PR3905 verifier (85 shorter words, 47 distinct elements, four-call formal endpoint and restoration controls).
- Genuine F4 and dual-number quotient characters distinguish the hypotheses; an eight-point noncommutative action preserves B.
- Separate AI review independently reconstructs both characters by different methods and rejects seven mutations in normal and optimized Python. No human or formal-kernel review is claimed.
- An 11-file regular-only, read-only, inode-disjoint Git-free export passes both commands. Commit-byte and declared source-history preflights pass. The published tree equals the tested local tree.

Reproduce: `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/sl2z-commutative-caller-obstruction`.

Credit 1337isnot1337 / OpenAI Codex (macbook-02) for PR3905 at b27bf4c72a822b21f483e08cb3241ad9d165b66f, and 1337isnot1337 / OpenAI Codex (codex2, laptop-02) for PR3914 at e44c63550d59173d7f5425b97c7fe22764214e0b. The A5 perfectness method also extends to commutative algebra images; this adds the distinct integer-shear relation and additive-carrier corollary. Retained model/domain context credits eumemic and huxint. New work by ToikY with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance.

Task bit-new-register-model, nonce 83ef8a01ed9fd7b72020c5a95f8d25ef, scope key 7084092dd726e7ba1f2f, is explicitly refined to this caller implication. Canonical main refreshed at 2026-10-19 05:07 UTC remains 20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90, priority revision 6. All 638 open PR bodies including drafts were checked and the repository overlap helper rerun. PR3905/3914 remain at the pinned heads; the new PRs concern a physical Gaussian transform and a conditional hosted receiver allocation; updated K492 CI repairs and the P104 head concern distinct contracts. No new matching caller obstruction was found. No existing PR for this branch was found.

Live Discussion access remains intermittent because of approval-service capacity failures; no complete Discussion coverage is claimed. The package records the original session's access limitations. The frozen package is unchanged; publication preflight confirms all 11 files still match the tested tree. Unchanged proof checks were not rerun just for publication. The initial selected binding-only baseline remains unverified because the sparse selected closure is unavailable; this scoped proof does not depend on that closure. No selected cold or native supplier replay is claimed.

Remaining obligation: specify and price a noncommutative native encoding, execution, decoding and arbitrary-dirty restoration for the same target, then establish its full supplier/recurrence inequality. Start with one complete four-call instance. The finite permutation control supplies no such bill. No continuing claim or larger word search is proposed.

title: Prove minimum binary carrier and native XOR bill for the integer-shear target
body:
PR3937 leaves open whether a noncommutative caller can preserve PR3905's integer-shear target B=X²Y². This package proves that the least binary module dimension detecting B is **three**, constructs the action through P1(F3), and prices its complete finite native endpoint. In the specified basis B is `b ^= c`: one XOR, with a second arbitrary dirty block untouched.

The representation preserves B but shortens the formal four-label expression to two labels. Each opaque label expands to two or three XORs, so the raw four/two-label bills are 10/5 XORs; cancellation gives the one-XOR native optimum. The separate literal M3(F2)-scalar boundary uses 18 dirty bits and three target XORs. There is no faithful encoding of the infinite source algebra, selected caller conversion, supplier inequality or new kappa. PR3905's original formal minimum remains valid.

## Scope and evidence

- Written universal proof: dimensions one and two kill B; the three-dimensional construction is a genuine action of the concrete integer group, not a proposed presentation.
- Source-bound verifier authenticates five retained files, checks all 576 SL2(F3) products, all 36 GL2 necessary-relation pairs, all 24 represented factors, and all 64 six-bit dirty inputs.
- Separate AI review reconstructs the action using a different implementation, classifies GL2 as S3, and searches all 168 GL3 truth tables to confirm the 2/3/1 XOR minima. It checks the complete columnwise 18-bit boundary and nine damaged-input cases normally and under optimized Python. No human or formal-kernel review is claimed.
- Registered CPython 3.12 replay passes. Final committed-byte, source-history and read-only Git-free export receipts are recorded in the handoff; hosted checks are separate and pending at publication.

Reproduce: `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/sl2z-binary-carrier` (standard library; recorded checks take seconds).

## Task and overlap

Base `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, priority revision 6. Picker `29f0b9b5b3f5e9f5ccf631f87e37932b`, track bit-mechanisms, card `bit-new-register-model`, scope key `7f5f4426ef796683c485`; refined to the released PR3937 caller handoff. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3937#issuecomment-6260657318).

Canonical main and relevant sources were refreshed before submission. The 05:57 UTC snapshot covered 649 open PR bodies including drafts, and the repository overlap helper was rerun. Live handoff prose and focused all-state searches were checked; complete Discussion/arbitrary-diff coverage is unclaimed. PR2599's full-stream faithfulness threshold, PR2620's GL2 actual-stream minima and PR2010's different SL2(F3) alphabet are credited and kept distinct. The selected orientation baseline remains unverified because its sparse closure is absent; no selected full cold replay is claimed.

## Credit and next question

Credit 1337isnot1337 / OpenAI Codex (macbook-02), PR3905 at `b27bf4c72a822b21f483e08cb3241ad9d165b66f`; ToikY / Codex, PR3937 at `5ee1c9cee717e682db01bff4c398b87011a135a2`; ywz65 / Codex, PR2599 at `cfafdd633cf4e2e534704ec3ddd684cb0c32734f` and PR2620; Cinna Davis / 1337isnot1337, PR2010. Retained source notices preserve their earlier attribution, including eumemic and huxint. New target-specific proof and checks by ToikY with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including separate AI review.

Stop this finite-carrier investigation here. A useful next step needs an actual payload subspace, injective encoder/decoder and consumer, with conversion, storage, all dirty roles and return priced. Target detection alone does not retain the formal tariff. No continuing claim, merge or selected-frontier change.

title: Research: exact fibre O(wV) invoice for PR2753 route_cube (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

[#2753](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2753) states that owner routes still use `O_q(wV)` implementations. This package binds that asymptotic charge to an exact, checkable fibre work invoice on the retained `routes.route_cube` bytes (vendor digest authenticated; PR2753 head `7dba5452a4071a856a0b11cebdcd2d3b6bcd7659` unchanged).

On the pinned routine, fibre payload `copy_bits` writes are exactly

| Regime | Partition calls | Fibre `copy_bits` writes |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `cap > 1` | `d² L` | `(2 d² L + 2) V` |
| `cap = 1` (`w = 1`) | `0` | `2 V` |

with `M = q^w`, `L = bit_length(M)+1`, `cap = M/q`, `H = cap^(d²)`, `V = H F`. For every checked `w ≥ 2` fixture this is at least `2 w V`, matching the stated `O_q(wV)` route charge on this reached primitive.

This answers open question 2 of `docs/research/selected-bit-caller-storage-map.md` for the **route** path only: an exact work lower bound on the retained decorated-key cube under complete-prefix order as implemented. It does not claim that every correct router needs `Ω(wV)`, does not replace the routine by an H2 primitive, does not price ordinary leaf `atom_swap`, and does not change the selected decimal.

**No new kappa.** Selected κ stays `0.001672660197076918`.

## Task and overlap

- Package: `research/pr2753-route-cube-owv-fibre/`
- Tip: `afcbc8468c9f0e154bca7557aadd562f5195c479`
- Base: `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`
- Scope: **refined** — exact fibre invoice for pinned `route_cube` only

Closest prior: merged [#2753](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2753) (recursive BIT caller and stated `O(wV)` baseline). Soft overlap ≈0.42: complementary exactification of the retained owner-route charge, not a ~0.9 retarget of `binary-digit-cost-audit` or `selected-route-live-volume`. Related [#2809](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2809) (physical caller), [#2708](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2708) (live-volume storage).

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/pr2753-route-cube-owv-fibre/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -Werror -B research/pr2753-route-cube-owv-fibre/verify.py
python3.12 -I -B research/pr2753-route-cube-owv-fibre/independent.py
python3.12 -I -B research/pr2753-route-cube-owv-fibre/test_package.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/pr2753-route-cube-owv-fibre
```

Expected:

```text
PASS_PR2753_ROUTE_CUBE_OWV_FIBRE fixtures=6 cursor_bits=[3, 5, 6, 8]
PASS_INDEPENDENT_PR2753_ROUTE_CUBE_OWV_FIBRE fixtures=6
PASS_PR2753_ROUTE_CUBE_OWV_FIBRE_PACKAGE_TESTS groups=6
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/pr2753-route-cube-owv-fibre outcome=completed
```

Default verify is read-only. Admission uses `need()` and still fires under `-O`. A temporary copy of `CERTIFICATE.json` with corrupted fibre totals is rejected, and duplicate JSON keys are rejected. `independent.py` does not import `verify.py`/`model.py`.

## Credit

Credit David Arias / [#2753](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2753) for the `O(wV)` route/leaf baseline and recursive caller, Jose Manuel / [#2697](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2697)/[#2809](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2809) for the routes/bitstream lineage and physical caller, Nick Petalas / [#2708](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2708) for route live-volume storage on the same decorated cube, and Arham Tahir (`linear-sign-total-traffic`) for closing linear-sign traffic and recording this route/leaf follow-up. Prepared by Wentao Li ([VictorLiwentao](https://github.com/VictorLiwentao), [@Is__Victor](https://x.com/Is__Victor)) with substantial AI assistance, under Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

1. Can an exact total-traffic invoice (key appends, `high_key` numerical work, Counter drains) replace the fibre-only lower bound? Fibre `copy_bits` already matches `O(wV)`; full tape traffic would sharpen bootstrap constants.
2. Does the ordinary leaf `atom_swap` path admit a similarly exact matching `Ω(wV)` invoice without retargeting `binary-digit-cost-audit`?

title: Research: price the first profitable helper-star interface word (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Add `research/r439-helper-star-threshold-20261018/`, a scoped positive
H2-sem specialization with a complete local boundary and cost invoice.

- For three targets each requiring the helper response `a+h`, direct writes
  cost 6 scalar ADDs. Preparing `h ^= a`, writing each target from `h`, then
  restoring `h ^= a` costs 5 and has the same exact arbitrary-dirty boundary.
- In general for this fixed transformation, the direct cost is `2q` and the
  wrapped cost is `q+2`; `q=3` is the smallest strictly profitable case.
- The 3-by-2 semantic response matrix `N` equals the required `K`; all helpers
  restore, every gate is zero-frame, and no target feeds a helper.
- The local positive bill is `{ADD1: 6}` versus `{ADD1: 5}`, with `F=B=3` for
  both the direct and wrapped words. Two malformed controls fail.

## Verification

- `python3 -B research/r439-bsection-stars-seed01/verify.py` —
  `PASS_R439_BSECTION_STARS` at the pinned base.
- `python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-helper-star-threshold-20261018`
  — registered replay passes all 64 binary dirty states in both directions,
  exact `N=K`, local F/B price and both controls.
- `python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-helper-star-threshold-20261018 --check-only`
  — `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`.

## Scope and overlap

Base: `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`; package commit:
`af918214331e99a92758fe8069ce3b3e285c25fc`. This is an abstract six-register

title: Conditional κ = 0.001734865178472710998233 (+0.00109%): pooled R438 slack across bit replicas on #3934, complex binds again
body:
Conditional κ = `0.001734865178472710998233 − 10⁻⁴⁶ − 10⁻⁷⁰`, which is **+0.00109% over #3934** (0.001734846264120199151475). **Draft: full verification is running.**

| | complex endpoint | bit endpoint | binds | κ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #3934 | 0.0017348651784727109982331 | R438 0.001734846264120199151475 | bit | 0.001734846264120199151475 − … |
| **this** | 0.0017348651784727109982331 | **pooled R438 0.001734900431583947157341** | **complex** | **0.001734865178472710998233 − …** |

## Idea

#3934 made the bit side bind at R438's endpoint. R438 is #1043's word with #2423's re-hosting. It leaves 54 width-8 slack units per replica, and its proven replica-local optimum is 10 empty capacity-42 copies plus one capacity-42 copy holding one residual (idle 34).

Pooling across the 32 replicas gives `32·54 = 345·5 + 3`. That makes the pooled32 optimum 345 empty 42-copies plus one empty 28-copy, with value 0.001734900431583947 (`bit-partial-width7-optimum`, k = 1 row). Both that package and seed72 leave open whether a **cross-replica owner map** can realize it. The complex T16 supplier already uses such maps (`owner_replica ≠ replica`).

This PR builds that map explicitly from R438's own placement. It makes 35 moves:
- the 32 single residuals (one per replica, child 6);
- the 3 residuals of one full capacity-28 copy of replica 0 (child 7, stages 5–8, inside child 6's window 3–8).

These go into 7 previously empty child-6 copies, five per copy. The idle bill changes by `{2:+7, 4:−1, 28:+1, 34:−32, 42:+25}`. Mass, child count and maxchild 42 are unchanged.

## Verification

`research/rank7-pooled-r438-bit/verify.py` runs in about 7 s and is independent of `build.py`.
- **Placement binding.** `ALLOC-R438.json.gz` matches `slot_list_sha256` in R438's rehost receipt on main.
- **Role audit.** All 126,144 roles are rebuilt and audited: windows, inactive host pairs, extents, cells, compact prefixes, and once-only hosting.
- **Baseline check.** The baseline equals the R438 certificate profile and endpoint.
- **Pooled endpoint.** It is accepted at c and rejected at c + 10⁻²⁴, with the fallback envelope.
- **Composition.** #3934's complex root is rechecked, and `κ = min(floor₂₄(complex), floor₂₄(bit)) − …`.
- **Controls.** 6 mutation controls are rejected.

`scripts/research_package.py` passes locally under Python 3.12. This PR stacks on #3934.

## Scope

New hypothesis: the bit supplier may use a cross-replica owner map. The slot rules are audited, but #1043's native hosted emission (C++17/Boost) has not been run. This is conditional on R438 (#1043 is open) and on the whole #3934 stack.

Credits: Ali Romman (#1043), Sagar Thakrar (#2423), mightyOil (#1281 pooled32 optimum), seed72/seed14 (windows, placement), #1023 (slot model), and the #3934 stack's credits, including OpenCode (Space bunny free). Prepared by Rohan Arun with Anthropic Claude assistance.

title: Research: no two-target UT4 word has n_b=7 with middle ranks (2,2) (n_b=7 open; no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Narrows the remaining gate left by [#3887](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3887). In the explicit `F_2[UT_4(F_2)]` central-target alphabet of [#1662](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1662), no legal word realizing two central targets — of any finite length, on any finite restored dirty workspace — has exactly seven paid `b` calls with middle ranks `(rank X, rank Y) = (2, 2)`, under the same unrestricted side-zero profile reduction used there.

At `n_b = 7` the #1662 rank bound permits patterns `(2,2)`, `(2,3)`, and `(3,2)`. The `(2,2)` slice still places every middle coupling in a fixed 2-plane, so interior dirty contractions cannot touch the side or `abc`/`cba` coefficients. Those equations reduce to a two-role unrestricted-profile census.

The census enumerates all 49,686 GL2-minimal zero-sum length-7 middle sequences, keeps the 49,140 with ranks exactly `(2,2)`, builds every side-zero transport key via a 3+4 meet-in-the-middle, and pairs keys for `abc = cba = I_2`. **Zero pairs survive.** A low-rank control with ranks `(1,2)` still produces pairs, so the screen is not empty by accident.

**Scope.** Middle ranks `(2,2)` only. Patterns `(2,3)` and `(3,2)`, and unrestricted `n_b = 7`, are left open. This does not claim that every `n_b = 7` word is impossible, does not restate the unit-tariff minimum 16 from [#1816](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1816), and does not reprint the `n_b = 6` census. No supplier or κ change.

**No new kappa.** Selected κ stays `0.001672660197076918`.

## Task and overlap

- Package: `research/ut4-two-target-nb7-ranks-22/`
- Tip: `4995b0ce91c163de821a5d117c6e5a5289c12172`
- Base: `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`
- Scope: **refined** — decide the `(2,2)` slice of `n_b = 7` only

Closest prior: [#3887](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3887) (`n_b = 6` impossible). The length-7 `(2,2)` census is the slice that PR left open; it is not forced by the length-6 result, because at `n_b = 7` the rank bound newly admits `(2,3)` and `(3,2)`.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/ut4-two-target-nb7-ranks-22/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -Werror -B research/ut4-two-target-nb7-ranks-22/verify.py
python3.12 -I -B research/ut4-two-target-nb7-ranks-22/independent.py
python3.12 -I -B research/ut4-two-target-nb7-ranks-22/test_package.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/ut4-two-target-nb7-ranks-22
```

Expected:

```text
PASS_UT4_TWO_TARGET_NO_NB7_RANKS_22 key_pairs=0 middles=49140
PASS_UT4_TWO_TARGET_NO_NB7_RANKS_22_INDEPENDENT key_pairs=0 keys_sum=46169088
PASS_UT4_TWO_TARGET_NO_NB7_RANKS_22_PACKAGE_CONTROLS checks=7
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/ut4-two-target-nb7-ranks-22 outcome=negative-result
```

Default verify is read-only. Admission uses `need()` and still fires under `-O`. A temporary copy of `CERTIFICATE.json` with corrupted pairs is rejected, and duplicate JSON keys are rejected. `independent.py` does not import `verify.py`.

## Credit

Credit @ToikY / [#1662](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1662) for the model and rank bound, [#1816](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1816) for unit-tariff exactness and the weighted open question, and [#3887](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3887) for the `n_b = 6` exclusion and the unrestricted side-zero reduction. Aaron Wang / @navinor / [#1690](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1690) for the profile/key pipeline. Prepared by Wentao Li ([VictorLiwentao](https://github.com/VictorLiwentao), [@Is__Victor](https://x.com/Is__Victor)) with substantial AI assistance, under Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

1. Does any two-target word have `n_b = 7` with middle ranks `(2,3)` or `(3,2)`? A middle rank of 3 escapes the fixed 2-plane argument used here.
2. Does any two-target word have unrestricted `n_b = 7`? That needs a dirty-role argument beyond the side-zero reduction.

title: Conditional κ = 0.001734846264120199151475 (+0.00176%): hosted remainders as receivers on #3251, complex passes R438 again
body:
Conditional κ = `0.001734846264120199151475 − 10⁻⁴⁶ − 10⁻⁷⁰`, **+0.00176% over #3251** (0.001734815770385098563484). This takes the whole remaining window to the R438 bit endpoint. **Draft: full verification is running.**

| | complex root lower | bit | binds | κ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #3251 | 0.0017348157703850985634843 | R438 0.001734846264120199151475 | complex | 0.001734815770385098563484 − … |
| **this** | **0.0017348651784727109982331** | R438 0.001734846264120199151475 | **bit** | **0.001734846264120199151475 − …** |

## Change

After #3251, 149,514 rank-1 idle remainders remain:
- 107,356 fail #1252's translation rule, so no receiver can take them.
- 39,558 conflict with every unhosted child of their group, and the group's other children are all hosted.
- 2,600 conflict with every unhosted child.

Relaying through an unhosted child was tested and found nothing legal.

New in this PR is a fifth phase: an idle-remainder axis may move into the remainder of **another partially hosted bin** in the same (replica, port). The axis must commute with that bin's **full** recipe frame (hosted prefix plus remainder), with all stage X/Y translations and the terminal Y translation, and with both terminal translations. Receivers are capped at 51, and no child both donates and receives.

This adds 2,374 moves, 437,978 in total, mostly merging pairs of rank-1 remainders into rank-2 children. Rank mass is unchanged at `65088·740`.

## Verification

title: Factor the restored P104 collector through one Newton query
body:
## Why this result matters

PR #3467 parametrized the larger stagewise P104 entrance, but its index did not establish what a restored caller can observe or whether the enlargement helps this collector. This package closes that logical interface and identifies exactly which coefficient directions reach Q.

Canonical investigation: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2750#discussioncomment-19010968

## Established result

For the declared PR #3467 coefficient encoder K, append the actual 257-event producer cone, the actual 15-event first collector, a 252-event selective producer inverse, and K inverse. The core has 524 events; after the codec inverse, all 52 coefficient banks, all five dirty D banks, and all 58 public frames return, with private C erased at zero. Both codec directions are additional to the core inventory. The resulting update is

$$
Q_{\mathrm{out}}=Q_{\mathrm{in}}+E_9(a_2+a_9+a_{16}+a_{27}+a_{51}).
$$

The return omits exactly the five inverse Q compensation ADDs. Full reversal would incorrectly add the initial dirty-D sum; the literal check verifies that adverse control on all 512 coordinates.

This answers three connected questions:

1. **The larger entrance adds no five-readout range.** With L the inherited stagewise entrance and S=(4B9)^52, both map onto B9^5 under the same five group-sum readout. A common explicit terminal-source section gives L/S isomorphic to ker(rho5|L)/(S intersect ker(rho5|L)), of size 2^86072. Every relative class has a kernel representative. rho5 itself does **not** descend to L/S, since rho5(S)=B9^5.
2. **The source-derived caller can close with dirty restoration.** The specified selective inverse supplies the exact returned-state contract and the Q update above. This is a newly appended logical return, not an assertion about an existing full-word return.
3. **That caller factors through one Newton query.** Two strict register schedules gather the five terminal coefficients, apply E9, add to Q, apply E9 inverse, and ungather. All 52 original coefficients remain returned outputs; invisible directions are not erased or released storage.

The five-readout map has Gaussian-array rank 2,560 and the final increment rank 512, with respective coefficient kernels of ranks 24,064 and 26,112. These are observation dimensions, distinct from the source program's native recipe rank mass.

| Rank-nine strict real arithmetic | Owned zero Gaussian bank | Temporarily mutable terminal bank |
|---|---:|---:|
| ADD/SUB excluding doubling | 43,520 | 41,472 |
| Explicit doublings | 2,304 | 2,304 |
| Checked exact halves | 4,608 | 4,608 |
| Extra Gaussian banks | 1 | 0 |
| Separate real zero scratch words | 1 | 1 |

If doubling is charged as one ADD, the ADD totals are 45,824 and 43,776. Both schedules restore their work storage. Conservative component bounds are 67,260H for non-query arithmetic and J+16,815H for Q. COSTS.md separates these strict schedules from the source core's incomplete native/component inventory; it does not infer a physical speedup from unlike tariffs.

## Evidence and review scope

Public result commit: **9f225dda71c45e2e6fea70e2ff5ef9f27192e1f9**. Retained-source ancestor: **9e501ba770d31c9f3decd51c987081c3b0acd256**. The public trees exactly match the locally tested trees. Only publication source-history pins and their receipt binding changed during publication; the scientific inputs, implementations, proof, costs, and original predecessor bytes stayed fixed.

- Two separately constructed literal executions each check 524 core events and 184,832 completed literal/ideal pairs. Full prepared/returned Y, coefficient, dirty-D, cut, and Q arrays are compared before hashing. The primary reuses authenticated predecessors; the independent implementation imports no predecessor executable and separately constructs the actual Y paths.
- Both direct schedules agree with those full returned coefficient and Q arrays. Signed arithmetic, width, alias/ownership, zero-exit, malformed-input, source-integrity, and typed-receipt controls are explicit and remain active under optimized Python.
- Three preparation/readout/direct fixtures distinguish a source-bound Y91/Y90 nonterminal kernel direction, a terminal difference, and a five-active strong representative. These are not three additional full 524-event replays.
- Registered normal and optimized Python 3.12 replays pass. The actual public commit passes committed-byte and source-history checks for all 31 exported source files. The exact committed export passes its transport-integrity gate. Actual Git-free replay and hosted CI results are reported in the publication comment rather than prospectively marked passed here.

Receipt SHA256: `27cf939d8766ac4baa120117d738045c80f8bde285f91446945f52b0f81188a1`.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-restored-query --check-only
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-restored-query
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/p104-restored-query --ref 9f225dda71c45e2e6fea70e2ff5ef9f27192e1f9 --check-source-history
python3.12 -B scripts/export_research_package.py export --package research/p104-restored-query --ref 9f225dda71c45e2e6fea70e2ff5ef9f27192e1f9 --output /tmp/p104-restored-query.tar
python3.12 -B scripts/export_research_package.py check /tmp/p104-restored-query.tar
```

From the extracted Git-free export: `python3.12 -I -O -B research/p104-restored-query/verify.py`. The default verifier never rewrites its receipt.

## Boundaries and next obligations

This is a closed **logical coefficient caller**. It does not supply a physical caller with those coefficient meanings, arbitrary raw-Y admission, the original full 2,025-event prefix, the whole 5,398-event word, or the 675 external-port contract. Physical routing/control, zero supply, access and ownership pricing, strict native/codec lowering, and the complete recursive bill remain open. The inherited 599/584 unchanged-profile stop and selected kappa remain unchanged. No human mathematical approval, formal kernel proof, or complete multiplication theorem is claimed.

TASK.json and README.md give two conditional next questions: name a real physical caller for this exact returned-state interface; or name an additional required, legally framed and fully priced readout that detects the source-bound kernel witness. Stop if no such consumer is justified. This package does not reserve a broader census or supplier construction.

TASK.json records the handoff-first scope decision, complete open-PR checkpoint, subsequent bounded deltas, fresh canonical Discussion/hub checks and their coverage limits. No same-scope overlap was observed; this is not an exhaustive novelty claim.

## Predecessor credit

PR #3467 supplies the exact entrance, codec and inherited index; #3423 already establishes the rank-one port map; #3382 supplies the Newton exactness application. Nick Petalas's #3416/#3426 provide phase-correct covariance and the correlated entrance; #3449, #3466 and #3469 address distinct calibration, full-prefix and adapter obligations. Credit ywz65/#2586 for the frozen word/native lineage, Arham Tahir/#2665 for retention, Tekalign/#3025/#3218 for signed-floor and phase-sensitive checks, Ross Richardson/#3068 for the exactness-domain question, Jose Manuel and Vasek for the unchanged-profile stop, and the retained geometry/native/compiler contributors.
